key_insight: The lattice Boltzmann method can be viewed as a rule-driven information-processing machine whose physics-constrained updates generate macroscopic transport laws.
engineering_relevance: This perspective offers a framework for adding physics-based or learned components to LB models while preserving the structure needed for macroscopic behavior.
method: Interpret local relaxation followed by lattice shifting as iterated dynamics related to residual networks and transformers.
Identify three update properties sufficient for closed macroscopic laws, with the target determining the specific law.
Test the framework using random targets on a lattice and a traffic-trained network on a graph.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that random-target dynamics generate the transport law predicted by their moments, while the traffic-trained graph network generates its own conservation law.
watch_item: Non-conserved modes can lose damping without warning from the lattice-level macroscopic law, so macroscopic agreement alone may not establish stability.
